title: Air India and IHG Partner on Loyalty Program, Offering Triple Points Through December
excerpt: Maharaja Club members can now earn points at 7,100 IHG hotels worldwide, with a 3x launch promotion and two-way points conversion across both programs.
body:
• Maharaja Club members will earn 2 points per US$1 spent at most IHG properties worldwide, with a triple-points launch offer through December 2026
  • IHG One Rewards members can convert points to Maharaja Points at a ratio of 1,000 to 200, bridging the two loyalty ecosystems
  • The deal connects IHG's 7,100-hotel global portfolio with Air India's five-continent network, giving Indian travelers more ways to earn rewards on the ground
  • Maharaja Club has crossed 100 partner brands and logged 4.2 million loyalty transactions in FY2026 as Air India expands its post-Tata rewards ecosystem

Air India and IHG Hotels & Resorts have announced a loyalty partnership that connects the airline's Maharaja Club program with IHG One Rewards, creating cross-earning opportunities for members across both platforms.

The partnership, announced this week, allows Maharaja Club members to earn points on qualifying stays at IHG's portfolio of more than 7,100 hotels across over 100 countries. Members will earn 2 Maharaja Points for every US$1 spent at most IHG properties, with stays at Candlewood Suites, Staybridge Suites, IHG Residences, and IHG Army Hotels earning 1 Maharaja Point per dollar.

How the Points Exchange Works

The deal also runs in reverse. IHG One Rewards members, a pool of more than 160 million travelers globally, can convert their hotel points into Maharaja Points at a ratio of 1,000 IHG points to 200 Maharaja Points. The minimum exchange is 1,000 IHG One Rewards Points, with conversions processed through IHG's regional contact centers and credited within 60 business days.

To set up earning, Maharaja Club members need to add their nine-digit membership ID to their IHG profile and set Air India as their earning preference.

Triple Points at Launch

To mark the launch, Maharaja Club members who register for the promotion can earn 3x Maharaja Points on qualifying IHG stays between September 15 and December 31, 2026. The offer carries no blackout dates, giving members flexibility during the peak travel season.

"Maharaja Club is evolving alongside Air India's transformation, with a strong emphasis on creating richer experiences for our members beyond the flight itself."

— Sunil Suresh, Head of Marketing, Loyalty and E-commerce, Air India

India Growth Pipeline

IHG currently operates 53 hotels across seven brands in India, including Six Senses, InterContinental, Crowne Plaza, voco, and Holiday Inn. The company has 110 additional hotels in its development pipeline expected to open over the next three to five years, according to Travel and Tour World.

Sudeep Jain, IHG's Managing Director for South West Asia, said the partnership strengthens the reach and relevance of IHG One Rewards in India. "India continues to be one of IHG's most important growth markets," Jain said, according to BW Hotelier.

What It Means for Indian Travelers

For diaspora travelers who fly Air India on long-haul routes and frequently stay at hotel chains, the partnership offers a way to accumulate rewards on both sides of the journey. The earn rate of 2 points per dollar at IHG hotels is competitive with similar airline-hotel tie-ups, and the triple-points launch promotion adds an incentive to book IHG properties through the end of the year.

The deal fits a broader pattern in Air India's transformation under Tata ownership. Maharaja Club has grown its partner network to over 100 brands between FY2023 and FY2026, with members recording more than 4.2 million transactions across travel, hospitality, lifestyle, and everyday spending categories in FY2026 alone, according to Travel Trade Journal.

The partnership arrives as Air India works to rebuild its premium positioning against domestic competitors IndiGo and Vistara, and international rivals on key routes to North America, Europe, and Southeast Asia. A deeper loyalty ecosystem is part of that pitch, giving frequent flyers more reasons to stay within the Air India orbit.
